Thomas Edison (February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and 
businessman. He developed many devices that greatly influenced life around the world, including 
the phonograph, the motion picture camera, and a long-lasting, practical electric light bulb. He was 
one of the first inventors to apply the principles of mass production and large-scale teamwork to the 
process of invention, and because of that, he is often credited with the creation of the first industrial 
research laboratory. 
in his اختراع براءةEdison was a prolific inventor, holding 1,093 US patents .4 name, as well as many 
patents in the United Kingdom, France, and Germany. More significant than the number of Edison's 
patents, are the impacts of his inventions, because Edison not only invented things, his inventions 
established major new industries worldwide, notably, electric light and power utilities, sound 
recording and motion pictures. Edison's inventions contributed to mass communication and, in 
particular, telecommunications. These included a stock ticker, a mechanical vote recorder, a battery 
for an electric car, electrical power, recorded music and motion pictures.
